what.title: What is AQMath, How It Works & Why
what.lead: Privacy-first portfolio mathematics software for your own crypto portfolio data.
what.whatP:
AQMath is portfolio mathematics software — a calculator delivered as a service. You enter the assets, amounts and model parameters; it computes the result of Risk Parity, Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimization and volatility-weighted Dollar-Cost Averaging for exactly those inputs.

Non-custodial. Your data is sent to our calculation servers when you run DCA or Optimize and is not written to a database on the free tier. No exchange connection, no orders. AQMath gives no investment advice.
what.howP:
1. Enter your assets and amounts and your own target weights (or let the engine compute theoretical weights from 180-day historical volatility).

2. Click SYNC to load public prices — spot prices come from Binance’s public market data, with CoinGecko as automatic fallback. Read-only market data: no API keys, no account linking.

3. Use DCA Distribution to compute how a contribution amount you choose splits across the assets below their target weight, weighted by volatility and trend.

4. (Black) Run the AQMath Engine to compute theoretical weights from the full covariance matrix and KKT projection.
what.whyP:
Most portfolio tools either collect your data or offer only basic arithmetic. AQMath is different:

→ Established mathematics (Risk Parity, KKT) with documented formulas
→ Non-custodial — on the free tier your portfolio stays in your browser’s localStorage and requests are processed in memory
→ Transparent, auditable logic (no black boxes)
→ €999 / year — software licence, paid in USDC & EURC

Free tier: your balances are processed in memory and not stored in a database. Black stores your holdings under a hash of your key. No exchange API keys required. No data to sell.
what.closingP: A calculation should not depend on mood. AQMath computes with the same formulas every time. As drawdown deepens and downside volatility rises, the Deleverage Modulator computes a lower target exposure — continuously, by math you can audit line by line. What you do with a result is your own decision.
what.closingPunch: the math is yours to audit. the decisions are yours to make.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How does the engine calculate risk?
faq.a1: The Black engine uses a Variance Matrix, asset Covariance, volatility estimates, and KKT-style projection to calculate Risk Parity allocations where each asset contributes a controlled share of portfolio risk. You can audit the full mathematical model in our [Documentation].
faq.a2: We don't track your wallet and ask for no name or e-mail. On the free tier your token balances live only in your browser's localStorage; during DCA and Optimize, position data is sent to our calculation servers, processed in memory and not written to a database (technical server logs keep counts such as the number of positions and the DCA amount). With a Black key, your holdings (token, amount, entry price, APY) are stored on our server under a hash of your activation key to run your daily calculations and restore your table on a new device, and are deleted on request or when your key is deactivated (Privacy Policy §9). The only other record is a one-way hashed activation record with a hashed IP address. Read the full data flow in our [Documentation].
faq.a3: Black access includes the full engine — Risk Parity optimization, Deleverage Shield, DCA distribution, unlimited tokens, automated data pipeline, and the shared Black chat. It's a 365-day term with direct support from the team.
faq.q4: Why are market widgets separated from features?
faq.a4: Live markets are informational context: ticker data, Fear & Greed, BTC dominance, movers, and exchange status. They support decision-making but are intentionally separate from the product feature story.
faq.a5: When enabled, USDC acts as a stablecoin buffer inside your portfolio. Any surplus from hard caps or unallocated DCA budget flows into USDC instead of being lost. Toggle it OFF to treat USDC as a normal token.
faq.q6: How do I apply for Black access?
faq.a6: DM us on Telegram or Twitter. We review every applicant personally — Black access is €999 / year. No call required — send a message, we review and send your activation key within 48h. Payments accepted exclusively in USDC and EURC.
faq.a7: No. Black access operates exclusively on an annual licence model (the App and the Backtest are free). We do not offer monthly, quarterly, or semi-annual plans. EU consumers keep the statutory 14-day right of withdrawal — see the withdrawal notice; after that the annual term is firm and is not refunded pro rata on early cancellation.
faq.a8: No. AQMath is an analytical web application. We do not execute trades, manage funds, or provide software that interacts with crypto exchanges or smart contracts.
faq.a9: No. AQMath is a web application only. Any app using our name on iOS or Android is not ours and is not authorized.
faq.q10: Do Black keys track my IP address?
faq.a10: No — not in any readable form. A Black key is tied to one device/network so it can’t be shared, but we only ever store a one-way hash of your key and a one-way HMAC fingerprint of your IP. Neither can be reversed back to your real key or IP. It exists purely to enforce one-key-one-user and to rate-limit brute-force attempts — never for tracking or profiling. Full details are in Section 8 of our Privacy Policy.
faq.q11: Is there an automatic daily calculation or notification service?
faq.a11: Yes — with Black. The server runs your daily calculations (Deleverage Shield status and DCA split) once per day from your stored holdings and can send a notice to your device. To do that, your holdings are stored under the hash of your activation key — never under your name or wallet. Notifications are optional and based on your consent; stored holdings are deleted on request or when your key is deactivated. Full details are in Section 9 of our Privacy Policy.
faq.a12: Black users get access to a shared internal chat visible only to active Black members. Messages are pseudonymous (shown as a short code like B-XXXXXX, never your real key or IP), capped at 200 characters, and limited to the 20 most recent messages (older ones are automatically swept daily). You can clear your own messages anytime. The chat is stored server-side under the hash of your activation key and is deleted when your key is deactivated.

tldr.title: ⚡ READ THIS PAGE IN 60 SECONDS
tldr.p1: What it does: AQMath is a calculator. You enter your assets, amounts and model parameters, and it computes the arithmetic result of the documented model — for example how a contribution you choose splits across your inputs.
tldr.p2: What the Deleverage Shield is: a calculation module that computes a lower target exposure when drawdown and downside volatility in your inputs rise, and a higher one as they recover. It displays a figure; it does not act.
tldr.p3: How we handle your data: no e-mail or password accounts, no wallet connection. On the free tier your portfolio lives in your browser. Black stores your holdings pseudonymously on our server and deletes them on request.
tldr.glossary: Plain English: drawdown = how far a portfolio falls from its highest point. Sharpe = return earned per unit of risk — higher is better. risk parity = weighting tokens by the risk they add, not by their dollar size. DCA = investing a fixed amount on a regular schedule.

s1.title: 1. What is AQMath?
s1.p1: AQMath is portfolio mathematics software for crypto portfolios — a calculator delivered as a service. It implements established mathematical models (Risk Parity, KKT optimization, volatility-weighted allocation) and computes their results for the assets, amounts and parameters you enter, with a privacy-first architecture that keeps what we store about you to a minimum and tells you exactly what that is.
s1.p2: At its core, AQMath computes the arithmetic of a split: given the assets and amounts you entered and a contribution amount you chose, how does the contribution divide across your inputs under a volatility-weighted model? A naive split (equally) ignores that some positions are already above their target weight while others are far below. AQMath’s DCA engine uses proportional allocation, filtered through a DCA safety pipeline, and shows the resulting split relative to the theoretical weights for your inputs. Whether and how to act on a result is your decision alone.
s1.p3: The system operates on a hybrid architecture: your portfolio data (token amounts, entry prices, targets) is stored in your browser’s localStorage, while computationally intensive math (covariance matrices, DCA allocation planning, volatility analysis) runs on our backend engine. On the free tier nothing financial is written to a database; Black additionally stores your holdings under a hash of your key (Section 9).
s1.privP: AQMath’s privacy model is non-custodial by design: on the free tier the backend receives position data in memory during a single DCA request, computes the result and discards it. No database record of your holdings. Technical server logs keep counts such as the number of positions and the DCA amount. Your financial state lives in your browser’s localStorage — the exception is Black, which stores your holdings under a one-way key hash and deletes them on request.
s1.whoP: AQMath is built for users who want to calculate for themselves:
s1.who1: Users who enter their own data and want a transparent calculation of how a contribution they choose splits across their own inputs, under a documented model.
s1.who2: Users who prefer numbers over feelings and want to see weight deviations from their own targets as figures, then decide and act entirely on their own.
s1.who3: Privacy-conscious users who refuse to connect wallets, hand over API keys, or trust a centralized service with their portfolio data. AQMath requires zero accounts, zero wallet connections, and zero data sharing.
s1.who4: DeFi participants who hold tokens across multiple chains and wallets and need a unified view with quantitative allocation — without giving any single service visibility into their total exposure.
s1.who5: Risk-aware allocators who understand that a 30% position in a single altcoin is not “diversified” just because it has a high target — and want structural limits (hard caps, risk budgets, circuit breakers) enforced automatically.
s1.notBot: AQMath is not a trading bot. It does not execute trades, predict prices, or time the market. It is a mathematical calculator: it computes how a contribution you choose divides across your own inputs under a documented model — and then gets out of your way.
s1.tiersP: AQMath has two tiers. Both are software for mathematical calculation; neither places orders or gives advice.
s1.tiersFree: Free — no account, no key. The App (DCA distribution with the safety pipeline, live price sync, portfolio kept in your browser) and the Backtest (upload up to five price CSVs and replay the production engine, Proteus (v18), against Buy & Hold). Requests are processed in memory and not written to a database. The Backtest limits requests per IP address, which is held in memory only.
s1.tiersBlack: Black — €999 for 365 days, with an activation key. The full engine: Risk Parity / KKT optimisation, the Deleverage Shield, unlimited tokens, the automatic price pipeline, daily calculations with calculation notices, and the shared Black chat. Your holdings are stored under a hash of your key and deleted on request.
s1.tiersBuy: Black is sold one-to-one in a chat, not through a checkout. The data processed there (Telegram username, the wallet address you pay from, transaction ID, your consumer or business declaration) is described in Privacy section 12. Terms, withdrawal notice and Privacy Policy are linked in the footer.

s2.title: 2. System Architecture
s2.p1: AQMath uses a hybrid architecture that separates data ownership from computational power. Your browser owns the data; the backend owns the math. This is fundamentally different from traditional portfolio tools that store everything on centralized servers, creating a single point of failure and a tempting target for data breaches.
s2.dfP: Understanding the data flow is critical to understanding AQMath’s privacy guarantees. Every computation interaction follows the same pattern: your browser sends the minimum information needed, and the backend returns results without retaining any state on the free tier. The single documented exception is Black (Section 9).
s2.df1: User enters tokens + targets → stored exclusively in browser localStorage. No network request is made.
s2.df2: SYNC clicked → live spot prices are pulled from Binance’s public market data (CoinGecko as fallback) — read-only market data. Your holdings are never transmitted.
s2.df3: DCA Distribute clicked → positions (including amounts) and DCA budget are sent to the backend engine via a single HTTPS POST request.
s2.df4: Backend computes → the DCA engine builds a plan-based proportional allocation, filtered through the full safety pipeline. All computation happens in-memory. Nothing is written to disk or database.
s2.df5: Results returned → updated token amounts are sent back to the browser and written to localStorage. The backend discards the request data immediately after responding.
s2.cleanP: Before price data reaches the optimization engine, it passes through a multi-stage cleaning pipeline that ensures mathematical integrity. Raw market data from multiple sources (CoinGecko, Kraken, Coinbase, MEXC) is often noisy — containing duplicates, exchange-specific outliers, and occasional gaps. The cleaning pipeline applies four sequential filters:
s2.clean1: Deduplication — removes duplicate timestamps, keeping the latest entry per date.
s2.clean2: Outlier Removal — rejects prices that deviate several standard deviations from a 7-day rolling window, eliminating flash-crash spikes and stale quotes.
s2.clean3: Multi-Source Merge — when the same token is collected from multiple exchanges, the median price is used to eliminate exchange-specific bias.
s2.clean4: Gap Interpolation — fills gaps of 2 days or fewer using linear interpolation, preserving trend continuity.
s2.cleanP2: This pipeline runs daily at 01:00 UTC via a scheduled cron job. The result is a clean, continuous price series suitable for covariance and volatility calculations.
s2.zkP: AQMath’s privacy architecture is non-custodial by design. The backend processes your DCA request statelessly — it receives position data, computes the allocation for your inputs, returns results, and discards everything from memory. No persistent record of your holdings is created server-side on the free tier; Black stores holdings as described in Section 9:
s2.zk1: No portfolio or financial database exists unless you opt in — and even then only a pseudonymous record under your hashed key, deletable at any time (Section 9)
s2.zk2: No portfolio amounts are logged or stored server-side after a DCA response
s2.zk3: The app never collects wallet addresses, API keys, or identity information
s2.zk4: On the free tier the backend cannot reconstruct your portfolio — it doesn’t retain the data
s2.zk5: Your browser’s localStorage is the home of your financial state; Black keeps a pseudonymous copy of your holdings
s2.zkWhyP: In 2023–2025, multiple centralized portfolio trackers suffered data breaches exposing user holdings. With AQMath, even a server breach could expose only what you chose to sync — token symbols and amounts tied to an anonymous key hash, never your name, wallet, or exchange keys. Your financial sovereignty is guaranteed by architecture, not by promises.

s3.title: 3. Portfolio Tracking
s3.p1: Your portfolio is a collection of token positions that you enter and that are stored in your browser’s localStorage. For each token, AQMath tracks your holdings, target allocation percentage, current price, staking yield, entry price history, and DCA cost basis. Together, these parameters form the complete state of your portfolio and drive every calculation in the system — from allocation metrics to risk budget calculations. If you use Black, a pseudonymous copy of your holdings is stored server-side under your hashed key (Section 9).
s3.pmP1: Every time the UI renders or a DCA calculation runs, the system computes real-time metrics for each token. It measures how much each position is currently worth, what share of your total portfolio it represents, and how far it has drifted from your intended target.
s3.pmP2: The DCA engine uses delta — the dollar gap between a token’s current value and its target value — to order how the contribution is divided: tokens furthest below their target receive the largest shares. Safe-haven tokens (stablecoins) bypass this filter entirely and receive their computed share when you designate them.
s3.pnlP: Profit and loss is tracked against your cost basis — the true dollar-cost-averaged entry price across all purchases. As the DCA engine buys more tokens over time, it accumulates your cost basis and total tokens acquired, giving you an accurate average price and return percentage for each position.
s3.discP1: AQMath records, it does not decide: the engine computes a difference between your holdings and the theoretical weights, and you record what you have done yourself — nothing ever executes by itself. The Recording Meter tracks one thing: how promptly you record calculated differences in your holdings table the same day. It is a log, not a judge. Many people assume they record ~90% of them the same day and discover it is closer to ~60%.
s3.discP2: Each calculated difference carries a 12-hour recording window. Recording within the first hour scores 100%, and the score decays to 0% at the end of the window; a difference you never record counts as missed. Your overall rate is the average score across all resolved records, shown with a Recorded / Missed / Dismissed breakdown and a rolling window of your last 10 records. The history chart plots your recorded equity against a comparison curve (every difference recorded on time) on a fixed $10,000 baseline.
s3.discP3: You set your own same-day goal (50–100%, default 80%) — self-set friction feels completely different from an app grading you, and the bar is colored against your own number. Active reminders are opt-in and silent by default, so opening the app is never penalised. The meter counts only the records you already have; it adds no new server-side data beyond the pseudonymous record described in Section 9.

s4.title: 4. DCA Distribution Engine
s4.p1: The DCA engine is the heart of AQMath. Given a budget (e.g., $500), it determines exactly how to distribute that capital across your portfolio’s underweight tokens — not equally, not randomly, but proportionally to how far each token is from its target, adjusted for risk.
s4.p2: The engine builds an allocation plan without ever touching your actual tokens: it assigns each token a share of the amount in proportion to how far it sits below its target, adjusted for risk. Tokens that reach their target drop out and their share is redistributed to the rest. Every computed share must clear a per-token minimum (default $20) — any share that would fall below that floor is dropped and its amount re-computed across the remaining tokens, so the result contains no sub-dollar shares.
s4.howP1: Before any allocation happens, each token is evaluated through the DCA safety pipeline (see Section 5). Only tokens that pass all filters are eligible to receive DCA funds. The allocation then follows a simple principle: the more underweight a token is relative to its target, the larger share of new capital it receives — tempered by a risk adjustment that reduces allocation for highly volatile assets.
s4.howP2: After each round, cost basis and token counts are updated automatically. Over multiple DCA cycles, the engine naturally balances your portfolio toward its ideal allocation.
s4.smallP: When the DCA budget is very small, the engine allocates the entire amount to the single most underweight eligible token.
s4.smallWhyP: If a $20 contribution is split across 5 tokens, each share is $4 — likely below exchange minimums, with fees a significant percentage. The small-contribution rule allocates the full $20 to the token furthest below its target. Over several cycles the computed result balances across all tokens. The same logic applies to larger amounts: every computed share must clear a configurable per-token minimum (default $20) — any token whose share would fall below that floor is skipped and its amount redistributed to the tokens further below target, so even a $500 contribution produces no tiny sub-dollar shares.

s5.title: 5. DCA Safety Pipeline
s5.p1: AQMath implements a multi-layer safety pipeline for DCA allocation, designed around crypto market behaviour. A conventional rule would pause on a 10% dip — but in crypto, pullbacks of that size are routine. Each layer operates independently and in strict sequence. Note: This pipeline governs only how the DCA amount you choose is split — it does not reduce existing positions.
s5.apyNoteP: Staking APY is tracked per token and displayed in the portfolio table together with its yield gap versus the 10% self-sustaining threshold. It does not gate DCA eligibility: an underweight token with a high yield still receives allocation like any other underweight token.
s5.l1P: The circuit breaker halts all DCA distribution whenever the Deleverage Shield is in its defensive state — when market conditions have deteriorated enough for the shield to cut exposure to a defensive level. Because exposure is driven mostly by drawdown and downside volatility, it engages during any meaningful downturn, not only brief flash crashes, and stays paused through a sustained bear market. It resumes automatically once the shield’s exposure recovers.
s5.l2P: A per-token risk adjustment that reduces the computed share of high-volatility assets. More volatile tokens receive proportionally less of the amount, so they do not receive outsized weights even when they are furthest below target.
s5.l3P: Skips tokens currently trading above their 50-day simple average of closes. The computed share goes to tokens trading at or below their average, not to tokens in a rally.
s5.l5P: No single risky token can exceed a structural concentration limit. If allocation would push a token beyond this cap, the excess is trimmed and redirected to the surplus pool.
s5.l5ProP: The Black engine’s /optimize endpoint replaces the flat 20% DCA cap with volatility-adaptive limits: high-volatility tokens receive tighter caps, while low-volatility tokens can hold larger positions (up to 40%). Each token’s maximum weight is dynamically scaled based on how volatile it is relative to the most volatile token in the portfolio. Note: the flat 20% hard cap still applies to the DCA distribution engine for all tiers — the dynamic caps only govern the Risk Parity weight computation.
s5.l6P: Total risky exposure is capped at a percentage of your portfolio, ensuring a safety buffer always exists. If risky tokens exceed the budget, all allocations are scaled down proportionally.
s5.l7P: All surplus capital from hard caps and risk budget scaling flows into your designated stablecoin. This capital sits in a safe buffer until you decide to redeploy it through DCA.

s6.title: 6. Volatility Calculation
s6.p1: Volatility is the foundational risk metric used throughout AQMath. It feeds into the safety factor, the Deleverage Shield's downside detection, and (in Black) the covariance matrix. The system computes a rolling volatility estimate for each token by measuring the magnitude of daily price swings — a standard approach in quantitative finance.
s6.pvP: Portfolio-level volatility is computed from the covariance matrix of token returns: σ = √(w'Σw), where w is the weight vector and Σ is the covariance matrix. Safe-haven tokens and frozen positions are excluded since they have near-zero volatility by definition. This portfolio-level metric drives adaptive thresholds across the entire safety pipeline.
s6.covP: The Black engine computes a full covariance matrix estimating how assets move together. Two tokens with moderate individual volatility but high correlation (like ETH and SOL) have amplified combined risk. The optimizer uses this to ensure each asset contributes equal risk — preventing hidden concentration through correlation.

s8.title: 8. AQMath Engine (Black)
s8.p1: The AQMath Engine is the Black-tier optimization layer that sits alongside the DCA engine. While the DCA engine splits a dollar amount you choose, the AQMath Engine answers a different question: what are the theoretical target weights for the inputs you entered? It uses established quantitative methods (Risk Parity, covariance estimation, KKT projection) to compute the weights from first principles.
s8.p2: The engine runs a three-stage pipeline: it builds a full covariance matrix from 180 days of cleaned price history, solves for Equal Risk Contribution (true Risk Parity), and applies KKT projection with dynamic volatility caps to enforce structural limits.
s8.ercP1: Traditional portfolio optimization (Markowitz mean-variance) requires estimating expected returns — a notoriously unreliable process that amplifies estimation errors into extreme allocations. Risk Parity sidesteps this entirely by optimizing for equal risk contribution rather than equal weight or maximum return.
s8.ercP2: The ERC solver searches for weights where each asset contributes an equal share of total portfolio risk. The process works as follows:
s8.erc1: Each token’s risk contribution is calculated by multiplying its weight by its marginal contribution to overall portfolio volatility.
s8.erc2: The solver repeatedly adjusts weights — increasing allocation to tokens that contribute too little risk, decreasing those that contribute too much.
s8.erc3: Every adjustment step keeps the weights valid, so the search settles smoothly into a stable solution.
s8.ercP3: The result is a portfolio where BTC and a small-cap altcoin each contribute the same amount of risk — preventing any single asset from dominating your portfolio’s volatility profile, even if it has the largest allocation.
s8.kktP: The raw ERC weights may violate real-world constraints (e.g., a 35% allocation to a single token). The KKT projection step enforces structural limits through iterative clipping:
s8.kkt1: Dynamic per-token caps — each token’s maximum weight is computed from its volatility. The more volatile a token is compared to the rest of the portfolio, the tighter its cap. Stable, low-volatility tokens can hold up to 40%.
s8.kkt2: Allocation budget — the optimizer allocates exactly the total budget it is given, never more. Portfolio-level exposure calculation is handled separately by the Deleverage Modulator.
s8.kkt3: No shorts — weights are clipped at zero; a token can be excluded entirely, but never sold short.
s8.kkt4: Surplus redistribution — capital freed by capping is redistributed to uncapped tokens proportionally.
s8.kktP2: The projection runs iteratively until all constraints are simultaneously satisfied.
s8.corrP1: The engine computes a full NxN covariance matrix from 180 days of cleaned, aligned price history. This matrix captures not just individual asset volatility but how assets move together. Two tokens with moderate individual volatility but high correlation (e.g., ETH and SOL tend to move in the same direction 85% of the time) have amplified combined risk — a relationship that simple weight-based allocation ignores entirely.
s8.corr1: Covariance matrix — upper-triangle annualized covariances for all token pairs
s8.corr2: Top correlations — the 6 highest-correlated pairs, sorted by correlation strength
s8.corr3: Portfolio volatility — the aggregate annualized volatility after KKT projection
s8.corr4: Per-token diagnostics — ERC weight, KKT weight, risk contribution, volatility, dynamic cap, and capped status
s8.rpWhyP: A naïve equal-weight portfolio of BTC + SOL + DOGE allocates 33% each. But DOGE's volatility is roughly 3x BTC's, meaning DOGE contributes ~60% of total portfolio risk despite holding only 33% of value. ERC automatically corrects this: it would allocate ~55% to BTC, ~25% to SOL, and ~20% to DOGE — ensuring each token genuinely contributes one-third of the risk.
s8.shieldP1: The Deleverage Modulator is a continuous exposure calculation that computes a lower target exposure as portfolio drawdown and downside volatility rise — no indicators, no timers, no correlation gate. Unlike simple "pause DCA" rules that only stop the DCA split, the modulator calculates the whole portfolio — it scales down the weights of ALL positions proportionally and shows the share computed for stablecoins (USDC) as the regime deteriorates. It displays figures; it does not execute trades.
s8.shieldCalloutP: As the regime deteriorates, the modulator computes two things at once: (1) a lower target exposure, with the weights of all token positions scaled down proportionally; (2) the allocation of the DCA amount to USDC while the Shield status is active. A calculation that only pauses the DCA split while leaving exposure unchanged through a -80% drawdown is not a shield calculation — it’s just a pause. AQMath shows these figures; it does not execute any trade.
s8.shield1: Two-signal regime read — the engine tracks only rising drawdown and rising downside volatility over a short rolling window. No moving averages, no timers, no correlation gate.
s8.shield2: Continuous scaling — target exposure is a smooth 0–100% dial that turns down as drawdown and downside volatility rise — not a set of discrete steps. The formula has no hard floor: in a deep, volatile crash exposure can approach zero. A 5% structural buffer (risk budget capped at 95%) ensures a minimum stablecoin allocation always remains.
s8.shield3: Capital preservation in simulation — while the Shield status is active the simulated portfolio holds the majority in cash-equivalent (USDC), absorbing only a fraction of the simulated decline. Exposure scales continuously with the regime, holding cash when drawdown and downside volatility are elevated.
s8.shield4: Steady ramp, fewer changes — computed exposure moves smoothly toward its target every bar, whether falling or recovering. To avoid over-trading in the simulation, Aegis (v14) only rebalances when the target drifts meaningfully from the simulated position — this deadband (not a slower re-entry) is what prevents whipsaw and keeps simulated trading costs low. DCA amounts allocated to USDC return to tokens in the calculation once exposure recovers.
s8.shieldP2: The shield’s effect in the simulations comes from asymmetric drawdown math: in a simulated -80% market decline, a portfolio with minimal exposure loses only a fraction of that decline. When the simulated market recovers, the preserved base compounds — which is why the backtests show better long-term results than holding through the full decline. This is a statement about historical simulations, not a prediction.
s8.vsBhP1: The chart below compares the live production shield, Proteus (v18), against a classic Buy & Hold strategy, measured through the exact production path: a rolling 180-day window re-read every day, the same 180-day strategic re-optimisation cadence the live service runs, shield state persisted from one interval to the next, and turnover charged at the live fee rate. This is deliberately not a continuous full-history replay — production never sees one — so these are the figures a live deployment would actually have produced. Both legs receive identical inputs and identical DCA treatment. The shield is scored on risk-adjusted return (Sharpe and Calmar) and on peak-to-trough drawdown, not on raw dollars.
s8.vsBhP2: Under half the drawdown, at a better risk-adjusted score. On a large-cap basket run through the exact production path, Proteus (v18) held peak drawdown to 23.1% against 55.9% for Buy & Hold — a 32.8-point reduction — while scoring higher on both risk-adjusted measures: Sharpe 1.63 vs 1.37 and Calmar 2.00 vs 1.23. On a high-volatility alt basket it cut peak drawdown from 59.8% to 29.4% and beat Buy & Hold on Calmar (1.29 vs 1.23). Exposure is a continuous 0–100% dial: it moves smoothly toward its target every bar in either direction, and redeploys parked USDC automatically as exposure recovers. Aegis (v14) adds threshold rebalancing — a deadband that skips trades when the target barely moves, slashing fees without changing the signal. There are no timers, no tranches, and no correlation gate.
s8.vsBhP3: Honestly scoped: this does not beat Buy & Hold on raw dollars, and on the alt basket it does not beat it on Sharpe either. Buy & Hold ends both samples higher in absolute value because it stays fully exposed through the bull run (large-cap CAGR 68.7% vs 46.2%; alt 73.2% vs 37.9%), and on the alt basket its Sharpe is higher too, 1.18 vs 1.10 — there Proteus wins Calmar and halves the drawdown, but it does not win the risk-adjusted race outright and we are not going to imply otherwise. The shield’s edge is drawdown and consistency, not terminal wealth. Out-of-sample, stated correctly: on a sealed second half of an earlier 5-token survivor basket never used to choose the Aegis (v14) preset, Aegis still cut peak drawdown from 63.2% to 25.3% — that result reproduces. Its Sharpe on the same sealed half was lower than Buy & Hold’s, 0.24 vs 0.30; an earlier version of this page reported those two figures the other way round, and that was wrong. Methodology note: that earlier basket is composed of tokens that survived to today (survivorship bias); see the stress test in section 8.6. Past results do not guarantee future performance.
s8.testingP1: The Deleverage Shield was measured on real market data, not hand-guessed. Every figure in section 8.5 comes from replaying the exact production path — a rolling 180-day window, the live strategic re-optimisation cadence, persisted shield state and turnover at the live fee rate — over two baskets, scored on drawdown, Sharpe, Calmar and CAGR. Earlier versions of this page quoted a continuous 8.7-year replay instead; that frame measures something production never does and its headline figures no longer reproduce from current data, so it has been retired rather than re-quoted.
s8.testingCalloutP: Over 2,095 daily intervals (~5.7 years) on a large-cap basket and 2,316 intervals (~6.3 years) on a high-volatility alt basket, replayed through the exact production path, Proteus (v18) held peak drawdown to 23.1% against 55.9% for Buy & Hold on large-caps, and 29.4% against 59.8% on alts. It beat Buy & Hold on Sharpe on large-caps (1.63 vs 1.37) but not on alts (1.10 vs 1.18), and it beat its own fixed-threshold predecessor on Sharpe, Calmar and maximum drawdown on both baskets. Both engine selections passed their ship gate.
s8.testing1: Signal construction — each bar we compute rolling drawdown from the running equity peak and downside volatility over a short rolling window, then map each to a 0–1 signal.
s8.testing2: Exposure rule — the combined risk signal drives a continuous exposure dial with no hard floor and no correlation gate.
s8.testing3: Hysteresis + threshold rebalancing — exposure moves smoothly toward target every bar in either direction, and Aegis (v14) only trades when the target drifts meaningfully from the held position — fewer rebalances with an identical signal. Parked USDC redeploys once exposure recovers.
s8.testing4: Engine/backtester parity — the live engine and the backtester run the same shield function on the same drawdown definition, so the public comparison is measured on one basis rather than two.
s8.testingAuditP: The shield is validated through the following checks on the production path:
s8.testingAudit1: Formula parity — the live engine and the backtester call the same shield function on the same drawdown definition (the window-local basket curve), so neither leg of the public comparison is measured on a basis the other cannot see.
s8.testingAudit2: Drawdown reduction — on the production path, peak drawdown cut from 55.9% (Buy & Hold) to 23.1% on the large-cap basket, and from 59.8% to 29.4% on the alt basket.
s8.testingAudit3: Risk-adjusted return — large-caps: Sharpe 1.37 → 1.63 and Calmar 1.23 → 2.00 versus Buy & Hold. Alts: Calmar 1.23 → 1.29, but Sharpe 1.18 → 1.10, lower than Buy & Hold — stated here because it is the one metric the shield loses.
s8.testingAudit4: Threshold rebalancing — a steady smooth ramp in either direction, trading only on meaningful exposure drift, confirmed with no whipsaw.
s8.testingAudit5: Out-of-sample check (Aegis v14, historical) — on a sealed second half of an earlier 5-token survivor basket, never used to pick the preset, Aegis (v14) cut peak drawdown from 63.2% to 25.3%; that result reproduces. Its Sharpe on the same half was 0.24 against Buy & Hold’s 0.30 — lower, not higher. This page previously reported those two Sharpe figures reversed, and previously reported a full-sample CAGR that no current run produces; both corrections are deliberate and unfavourable to us. That study ran a retired v14 preset, so it is historical context rather than a current claim, and a fuller walk-forward multi-fold study is still worthwhile.
s8.testingAudit6: Survivorship stress (dead token) — the earlier basket is all survivors, which flatters both legs. Re-run on a window opening at Terra Classic’s April-2022 peak with LUNC (which fell from ~$121 to ~$0) added, Aegis (v14) held peak drawdown to 20.8% against 24.7% for the survivor-only basket — the defense did not degrade — while Buy & Hold worsened from 63.2% to 70.7%, a 7.5-point deterioration, and the shield still cut drawdown by ~50 points on that window. An earlier version of this page said Buy & Hold worsened by “up to ~18 points”; the measured figure is 7.5. Same retired v14 preset, so historical context (and raw return figures remain flattered by crypto’s post-crash rebounds).
s8.nextgen: LIVE ENGINE The deployed shield is Proteus (v18), a volatility-adaptive engine. Every figure in sections 8.5 and 8.6 is measured on the exact production path — a rolling 180-day window, the same 180-day strategic re-optimisation cadence, and persisted shield state — so the two sections describe one study, not two. Against its fixed-threshold predecessor Aegis (v14) it cut maximum drawdown on both a large-cap basket (25.7%→23.1%) and a high-volatility alt basket (36.8%→29.4%), with a higher Sharpe and Calmar. Aegis (v14) now runs only as a warm-up fallback, for portfolios with too little history for the adaptive threshold to calibrate; where v14 appears above it is labelled as historical.

s9.title: 9. Privacy & Data Separation
s9.p1: AQMath’s privacy is not a feature bolted onto the product — it’s the foundational architectural principle. The system is designed so that your financial data is mathematically isolated from the computation layer.
s9.backendTitle: 🟢 Backend Receives (ephemeral — plus opt-in stored data)
s9.backend7: Backtest price series (CSV you upload) — processed in-memory, then discarded
s9.backend8: Black: holdings and daily calculations (stored, deletable): token symbols, amounts, entry price, APY and the frozen weight plan, under the hash of your key
s9.backend9: Consent receipts and must-read acknowledgements — GDPR audit records
s9.backend10: Notification setup — a random unguessable topic; the read token is stored only as a hash
s9.backend11: Black chat messages (stored, deletable): pseudonymous messages (≤200 chars) under the hash of your key, rolling cap of 20 messages + daily sweep of the oldest
s9.bnP: This is the most critical section. The following data is architecturally impossible for the backend to access:
s9.bnCtP: On the free tier, no database table maps users to portfolios and no log records your holdings. The exception is Black (Section 9): holdings, the frozen plan and consent receipts are stored under the one-way hash of your activation key — never your name, wallet, or exchange keys. Technical server logs keep counts such as the number of positions and the DCA amount, not your token list.
s9.t1b: Never entered — AQMath doesn’t connect to wallets
s9.t2b: Never requested — price sync uses public endpoints
s9.t3b: Never transmitted — only current state during DCA
s9.t4b: No accounts, no email, no registration
s9.t5b: Sent during DCA and not stored by the DCA service; Black stores it with your holdings
s9.t7b: Sent during DCA, not stored by the DCA service — Black stores APY with your holdings (UI bookkeeping)
s9.t8b: Never your raw key — everything is linked to a one-way hash; no name, email, or wallet
s9.bnP2: The backend processes your DCA request in a single HTTP round-trip: receive positions → compute allocation → return results → discard. On the free tier there is no database table that maps users to portfolios (Black is the exception: holdings stored under the hash of your activation key). Technical server logs keep counts such as the number of positions and the DCA amount, not your token list.
s9.zkP: AQMath implements a practical non-custodial privacy model:
s9.zk1: The backend shows its work through detailed split summaries (e.g., “BTC: +$142.30 (0.002371 tokens)”) so you can check the arithmetic yourself.
s9.zk2: The DCA service does not store the inputs. After the HTTP response is sent, the request data is released from memory. No disk write. No database insert. (Black stores holdings as documented in Section 9; server logs keep technical counts.)
s9.zk3: The browser verifies the results by applying updated amounts and re-rendering the portfolio.
s9.zkP2: The backend does not retain your data after the HTTP response is sent — request data is garbage-collected from memory with no disk write, no database insert, and no logs of your holdings. Your portfolio lives in your browser’s localStorage — the only server-side mirror is the pseudonymous one you opt into (Section 9).
s9.compP: Traditional trackers store everything on centralized servers — one breach exposes all users. AQMath stores nothing by default; the only stored data is what you opt into — pseudonymous and deletable. No accounts, no wallet connections, no analytics tracking.
s9.c1c: Browser localStorage; Black: pseudonymous holdings data
s9.closing: AQMath gives you the computational power of a quantitative hedge fund’s allocation engine while maintaining the data sovereignty of a paper notebook.
s9.chatP1: Black users have access to a shared internal chat visible only to active Black members. The chat is designed for direct communication between Black members and the team — no automated onboarding, no helpdesk.
s9.chat1: Pseudonymous: messages are shown under a short code (e.g., B-XXXXXX) derived from the hash of your activation key. Your real key, IP, and identity are never displayed.
s9.chat2: Rolling buffer: only the 20 most recent messages are kept. The oldest message is additionally swept once per UTC day.
s9.chat3: 200-character limit per message, with a 3-second cooldown between posts to prevent flooding.
s9.chat4: Deletable: you can clear your own messages anytime via the Clear button. Deactivating your Black key deletes all your chat data.
s9.chatP2: The chat is stored server-side in the same pseudonymous manner as Black holdings — under the one-way hash of your activation key, never under your name or wallet.
s9.backend12: IP address — held in memory only to limit request rates, never written to a database
s9.t9b: Handled outside the app (Telegram): username, payment wallet address, transaction ID — see Privacy section 12; the app never sees them

bt.intro: Upload historical price CSVs for your tokens (up to 5). Every run executes the production engine — Proteus (v18), volatility-scaled dynamic thresholds with V-bounce re-entry — on your basket, capital and DCA schedule, next to Buy & Hold, which buys tokens unconditionally and stays fully exposed. The basket follows the same 180-day macro loop as production — a KKT risk-parity re-optimisation every 180 days on the trailing 180-day window. Both legs charge the same simulated fees and redeploy parked DCA cash the same way, and results are scored on risk-adjusted return (Sharpe and Calmar), not on beating Buy & Hold.

The former Aegis (v14) comparison leg is retired from the backtest; v14 still runs in production only as a warm-up fallback for portfolios too young to calibrate the adaptive threshold.

shield.lead: Proteus (v18) scales exposure continuously off a volatility-adaptive drawdown threshold — no indicators, no timers, no correlation gate. It ramps exposure toward its target steadily in either direction, and only rebalances when target exposure drifts meaningfully.
shield.body: Replayed through the exact production path — a rolling 180-day window, the live re-optimisation cadence, persisted shield state and turnover at the live fee rate — Proteus (v18) held peak drawdown to 23.1% against 55.9% for Buy & Hold on a large-cap basket, at Sharpe 1.63 vs 1.37 and Calmar 2.00 vs 1.23. On a high-volatility alt basket it cut drawdown from 59.8% to 29.4% and won Calmar (1.29 vs 1.23) — but lost Sharpe there, 1.10 vs 1.18, and Buy & Hold ends both samples with more dollars. The shield’s edge is drawdown and consistency, not terminal wealth. On a sealed out-of-sample second half of an earlier survivor basket, Aegis (v14) still cut drawdown from 63.2% to 25.3%, but its Sharpe was lower than Buy & Hold’s (0.24 vs 0.30) — an earlier version of this page had those two numbers the wrong way round. Backtest baskets include survivor tokens; past results don’t guarantee future performance.
shield.nextgen: LIVE ENGINE Proteus (v18) is the production shield. Aegis (v14), its fixed-threshold predecessor, still runs as a warm-up fallback for portfolios too young to calibrate the adaptive threshold; where v14 figures appear on this site they are labelled as historical. The figures above are measured on the exact production path, not on a continuous full-history replay.

lp2.heroTitle: Portfolio mathematics you can audit line by line.
lp2.heroDesc: AQMath calculates Risk Parity, Karush–Kuhn–Tucker optimization and volatility-weighted dollar-cost averaging for the assets and parameters you enter — on its own servers. No e-mail accounts, no wallet connection.
lp2.does1: Recomputes the covariance matrix across your holdings on every cycle.
lp2.does2: Reads the drawdown and downside-volatility regime continuously. No indicators, no timers.
lp2.does3: Computes a lower target exposure toward stablecoins as risk rises, and a higher one as it clears.
lp2.doesNote: The calculations run on our servers. Free: your portfolio stays on your device and requests are not saved to a database. Black: your holdings are stored on our server under a hash of your key, to run your daily calculations.
